Every aiui server publishes an OpenAPI 3.1 document of its own HTTP API, and the app shell has a page to read it and send requests. Nothing to configure: both are on by default. GET /api/openapi.json is built from the route table the server is running, when it is asked. It lists every API route it answers (/api/*, /v1/* and the unprefixed data routes such as /sessions and /run): the core, each enabled built-in, and the routes of your plugins and register_feature() features. It cannot go stale, and a built-in you switch off (extensions: {disabled: [builtin.training]}) leaves it. Field Comes from tags The built-in that owns the route (sessions, api, config…), a plugin's or feature's name, else core summary, description The handler's docstring: first line, then the rest (plain text; a leading POST /path — is dropped) parameters Path parameters and their types ({id:int} is an integer) security Bearer token; [] on the public routes (/api/health, sign-in) servers /: the server that served the document x-websockets The WebSocket routes (/api/chat/ws, /api/logs/stream) The route needs the same credentials as every other /api route in each auth mode. A plugin the caller may not use (an entry-point plugin that is off by default on a remote or sign-in server) is left out. Switch the document and the page off with extensions: {disabled: [builtin.api-reference]}. Use it anywhere an OpenAPI file goes: client generators, API tools, or the API reference of an aiui docs site (api: {openapi: http://localhost:8000/api/openapi.json}, see OpenAPI).

A feature adds request bodies, responses or anything else to its operations with an optional openapi() method, keyed by "METHOD /path": The OpenAI-compatible routes (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/embeddings…) carry their request bodies this way.

In the app shell (style: app), API Reference in the Control group (/api-reference) shows the routes by feature with a search box (method, path or text). Pick a route to read it and try it against this same server: fill in the path parameters, a query string and a JSON body (prefilled from the document's example); Send request shows the status, time and the response, pretty-printed; Copy cURL gives the same request for a terminal, with $AIUI_TOKEN in place of a token; OpenAPI JSON downloads the document; ?op= opens one route (/api-reference?op=get_api_sessions). Requests go to the same origin with your session, so no proxy, CORS setup or pasted key is needed. The default dashboard style is unchanged; its Inspector and API pages stay.
